top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Germany's far-right AfD won the Saxony-Anhalt state election with nearly 44 per cent and is courting individual conservative lawmakers to form what would be the first far-right state government in postwar Germany; Chancellor Friedrich Merz ruled out cooperation but admitted the result had shaken his party to its foundations. The Middle East hardened on two fronts at once - Israel's defence minister threatened 'full-scale war' against the Palestinian Authority hours after strikes on the Lebanese town of Kfar Rumman killed at least 11. The Gulf's answer was the quieter surprise: the UAE and Qatar both said publicly that they can no longer rely on Washington alone for their security, as Iran warned that American energy assets in the region are 'exposed'. Much of the rest of the day was damage - a volcanic eruption stranding about 270,000 travellers in Indonesia, a fatal cargo-jet crash in Miami, an avalanche, a building collapse. Watch Saxony-Anhalt: whether any conservative lawmaker breaks the 'firewall' matters well beyond one German state.

stories.headline: Far-right AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt with nearly 44% as Merz rules out cooperation
stories.summary: The Alternative for Germany took first place in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt with close to 44 per cent of the vote, winning 39 of 83 seats - short of a majority - and is now appealing to individual conservative lawmakers to help it form the first far-right state government in postwar Germany. Chancellor Friedrich Merz ruled out any cooperation but conceded the result had shaken his Christian Democrats 'to its very foundations'. France and Poland both voiced alarm; the party wants to deport immigrants, halt support for Ukraine and restore ties with Moscow.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes on a southern Lebanese town kill at least 11, Lebanon's news agency says
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes hit a residential building in Kfar Rumman just after midnight, killing nine people including two children, and a separate drone strike on a civilian vehicle in the same town killed two medics, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. No online evacuation warning was issued beforehand. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to questions about the strikes; it has said recent operations targeted Hezbollah weapons stores and a command centre. At least seven people were killed in Israeli strikes in Lebanon the previous day, despite a June ceasefire.
stories.source: The Straits Times, BBC (Lebanon's National News Agency)

stories.headline: Israel threatens 'full-scale war' against the Palestinian Authority
stories.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz said he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had instructed the military to prepare for a full-scale war against the Palestinian Authority if its security bodies initiate an Oct 7-style attack on Israeli forces or settlements. He said the campaign would target the Authority's senior leadership in Ramallah and include targeted killings and a permanent military presence in areas residents would be evacuated from. The remarks followed a stabbing attack in the northern occupied West Bank in which the military said it shot the assailant dead.

stories.headline: Iran threatens US energy assets in the Gulf and plans a new restricted shipping zone
stories.summary: Parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, Iran's top negotiator, wrote that the region's oil and gas production chain is 'sprawling, accessible, and exposed' and that American energy companies share that exposure - 'strike our assets and you get struck'. It followed US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's warning that Iran's tanker fleet was 'defenceless'. Security official Mohsen Rezaei said Iran will announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf within days and add any ship entering it to a sanctions list. Oil touched six-week highs on Monday.

stories.headline: Gulf states say they can no longer rely on the US alone for security
stories.summary: UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash told the Hili Forum in Abu Dhabi that the country is building alternative pipelines, ports, railways and trade corridors so its energy exports are not 'held hostage' by the US-Iran war, and warned that rebuilding trust with Tehran could take decades. Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said at the same forum that a strategic alliance with Washington 'is very important but is not enough' and that self-sufficiency in security is the only way forward. Both criticised the Gulf's failure to mount a coordinated response.

stories.headline: Kremlin says it does not rule out restarting three-way peace talks
stories.summary: Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow does not rule out resuming the trilateral format with Ukraine and the United States, but that it is 'too early to speak of the venue and exact dates'. He was responding to the weekend visit by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv, and said a phone call between President Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump was also possible. Peskov declined to discuss the content of the latest US proposals or the hardest outstanding issues.

stories.headline: Kyiv is under more air raid alerts than at any point in the war, BBC Verify finds
stories.summary: BBC Verify's analysis of Ukrainian government figures found Kyiv recorded 76 air raid alerts in the seven days from 27 August, above the previous peak of about 66 in the week beginning 27 February 2022. Residents have had to shelter as many as 13 times a day, with individual alerts lasting from minutes to nearly four and a half hours, shutting schools and offices and halting overland trains. Ukraine's air force says Russia launched 2,800 jet-powered attack drones in August, almost twice July's total; some fly close to 595kmh.
stories.source: BBC Verify (Ukrainian government figures, Ukrainian Air Force)

stories.headline: UN rights chief calls for a ban on fully autonomous weapons after Ukraine drone deaths
stories.summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk told the Human Rights Council he was 'horrified by reports that fully autonomous drones launched by the Russian Federation killed three Ukrainians last month', and noted reports that Ukraine has field-tested such weapons too. He joined calls for an urgent prohibition on weapons that can kill without human involvement. On 5 September, 128 countries agreed a definition of autonomous weapons; governments decide in November whether to open treaty negotiations.
stories.source: The Straits Times, AFP (UN Human Rights Council)

stories.headline: UN rights chief warns advanced AI could pose an 'existential risk' to humanity
stories.summary: In a speech to the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva ahead of his second term, Volker Turk said he shared industry insiders' concerns that advanced AI could threaten humanity and called for 'cast iron guarantees' on AI safety and security 'before it is too late'. Without naming companies, he said a handful of men hold 'almost unlimited power over AI' and urged countries hosting AI and involved in its supply chains to agree red lines. The UN held its first global meeting on AI governance in July.

stories.headline: China to inject 360 billion yuan into state banks and insurers
stories.summary: Three state banks and five state insurers said they would raise up to a combined 360 billion yuan (about US$54 billion) through capital injections from the finance ministry and other shareholders, with the ministry issuing 300 billion yuan of special bonds to fund it. Banks take roughly 290 billion yuan, intended to preserve their capacity to keep lending as Beijing presses them to support activity; the five insurers share 70 billion yuan. It is the first time China has extended the special-bond tool to insurers.
stories.source: BBC, CNBC (Chinese finance ministry via Xinhua)

stories.headline: Anak Krakatau eruption leaves about 270,000 stranded as Indonesian airports extend closures
stories.summary: Airports across Indonesia extended closures because of volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau, leaving roughly 270,000 travellers stranded. With flights cancelled, passengers are turning to marathon overland journeys - train tickets have sold out and airfares on the routes still running have surged. Singapore's embassy in Jakarta has told Singaporeans there the situation remains 'fluid' with further disruption possible.

stories.headline: Nepal holds a national day of mourning for flash flood victims
stories.summary: Nepal observed a national day of mourning for those killed in the flash floods that struck late last month. Rescuers are still working through debris, with the search running alongside occasional survivor finds - a Chinese man was pulled from a tunnel 10 days after the floods. Nine Singaporeans remain missing; Singapore has sent more than S$560,000 in humanitarian assistance and deployed police officers to assist the search.

stories.headline: Seven dead in Delhi building collapse as rescuers dig through debris
stories.summary: Seven people have been confirmed dead after a building collapsed in Delhi, with rescuers still working through the rubble and others feared trapped. Emergency crews have been digging by hand and with heavy equipment at the site.

stories.headline: Five killed as an Amazon Prime Air cargo jet overran a Miami runway
stories.summary: Prime Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 operated by 21 Air and inbound from San Juan, overran a diagonal runway at Miami International Airport shortly before 2pm local time on Sunday and struck vehicles on the ground. At least five people died and five were injured, three critically, Miami-Dade Fire Chief Ray Jadallah said. More than 60 rescue units and about 200 personnel responded and crews spent the afternoon dealing with a fuel leak. Two of the airport's four runways reopened by Sunday evening; the FAA has opened an investigation.
stories.source: The Straits Times, BBC (Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, FAA)

stories.headline: Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,000 jobs as Europe's car sector stalls
stories.summary: Jaguar Land Rover said it would cut 4,000 jobs, the latest sign of strain across a European car industry contending with weak demand, the cost of the electric transition and trade pressure. The announcement lands alongside a broader run of retrenchment across the sector.

stories.headline: Russia and North Korea open their first road bridge across the border
stories.summary: Russia and North Korea opened the first road bridge linking the two countries across their short shared border. Moscow and Pyongyang have sharply expanded military and economic cooperation since Russia launched its offensive in Ukraine, and the crossing gives them a permanent overland link that does not depend on the existing rail bridge.

stories.headline: China's top court issues guidelines on deepfakes and AI disputes
stories.summary: China's Supreme People's Court published guidelines covering artificial-intelligence disputes, stating that people cannot use AI to create or distribute recognisable digital replicas of others without consent, including cloned faces and voices, state news agency Xinhua reported. The guidance gives lower courts a reference point as deepfake and likeness cases multiply.

stories.headline: Avalanche kills at least 11 climbers in Russia's North Caucasus
stories.summary: An avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi in Kabardino-Balkaria at about 5pm local time on Sunday, hitting a group of 33 climbers. Local emergency services said at least 11 people were killed and six injured; 10 climbers made their own way down and the fate of six others was still unknown on Monday morning. More than 50 emergency workers are searching, hampered by difficult terrain and a high risk of further avalanches.

stories.headline: German investigators find 21 explosive devices near power lines in Saxony
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Saxony said nine more homemade explosive devices were found over the weekend near high-voltage lines south of the Graustein substation in Goerlitz district, taking the total recovered to 21. Germany has been on alert since a run of sabotage incidents on the power grid last week, following an August drone attack at Leipzig/Halle that Berlin formally blamed on Russia. A man who sent letters claiming responsibility is still at large. A separate transformer fire in Berlin on Monday was attributed to a technical fault.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Saxony police and prosecutors)

stories.headline: Belgium detains a dual Chinese-Belgian national over semiconductor espionage
stories.summary: Belgian prosecutors said a 52-year-old man with dual Chinese and Belgian nationality has been in pre-trial detention since May on suspicion of illegally transferring intellectual property and trade secrets abroad. He formerly held a senior post at the Belgian gallium nitride chipmaker Belgan, declared bankrupt in July 2024, while allegedly also directing a Chinese company making the same chips, set up months after he joined Belgan and backed by a Chinese investment fund. He was arrested at Zaventem airport before a flight to Beijing; a second suspect is at large.

stories.headline: Thousands gather in Belgrade for Ratko Mladic's funeral
stories.summary: Thousands queued outside a Belgrade church to pay respects to the former Bosnian Serb general, who died last week while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. Free buses ran from Bosnia and most Serbian towns. Mladic was convicted by the UN tribunal over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, in which about 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed, and the 43-month siege of Sarajevo. EU enlargement commissioner Marta Kos postponed a visit to Serbia over what she called the 'glorification' of Mladic.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia to give the IAEA extra inspection powers short of the Additional Protocol
stories.summary: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said the planned US-Saudi civil nuclear agreement does not include Riyadh signing the Additional Protocol, which allows snap inspections at undeclared sites, but that provisions 'very, very similar' to it are being written into a bilateral agreement covering enrichment, uranium conversion and reprocessing. Non-proliferation groups had criticised the July deal for omitting the protocol. The bilateral text goes to the IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors once finalised.

stories.headline: Philippine president's lawmaker cousin charged over the flood-control scandal
stories.summary: A lawmaker who is a cousin of the Philippine president has been charged in connection with the flood-control corruption scandal, one of the most damaging political controversies facing the administration.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Parliament debates political salaries on Tuesday, with PM Lawrence Wong and Chan Chun Sing both delivering ministerial statements on the government's response to the latest review. The haze shapes the rest of the week: NEA expects air quality between moderate and low unhealthy on Tuesday as smoke keeps drifting in from Sumatra and Kalimantan, the Red Cross is distributing air purifiers and care packs, and Singaporeans in Indonesia have been told to e-register with MFA as volcanic ash grounds flights. The courts had a heavy day, from an upheld 11-year term for the Dunearn Road drink driver to a first tranche of seized luxury goods drawing S$1.3 million in bids. The talk, meanwhile, is dominated by the pyramid-scheme trips to Nanning and the fallout from last week's racist comments online. If ministerial pay matters to you, Tuesday's sitting is the one to follow.

stories.headline: Parliament debates political salaries on Tuesday, with PM Wong and Chan Chun Sing to speak
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister-in-charge of the Public Service Chan Chun Sing will deliver ministerial statements on Sept 8 setting out the government's response to the latest review of political office-holders' salaries. The debate is scheduled for the current parliamentary sitting week.

stories.headline: Ong Ye Kung says AI is replacing tasks, not entire jobs
stories.summary: Speaking to students and staff at the annual Kent Ridge Ministerial Forum at NUS, Health Minister Ong Ye Kung said artificial intelligence is displacing certain tasks within roles rather than eliminating whole occupations, and framed the job-market effect as a shift in what work looks like rather than a wholesale replacement.

stories.headline: NEA expects air quality to stay between moderate and low unhealthy on Tuesday
stories.summary: The National Environment Agency said moderate to dense smoke plumes from fires in southern and central Sumatra and West Kalimantan continue to drift towards Singapore, and forecast the 24-hour PSI to remain in the moderate to low end of the unhealthy range on Sept 8.

stories.headline: Singaporeans in Indonesia urged to e-register with MFA as volcanic ash disrupts flights
stories.summary: The Singapore Embassy in Jakarta advised Singaporeans in Indonesia to e-register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and to minimise outdoor activity, saying the situation after Mount Anak Krakatau's eruption remains 'fluid' with further flight disruption possible. Several Indonesian airports remain shut because of ash.

stories.headline: Singapore Red Cross steps up heat and haze support with air purifiers and care packs
stories.summary: The Singapore Red Cross is distributing air purifiers and support packs to vulnerable households as the haze and heat persist, alongside assistance with utility bills for families who need to run fans or air conditioning for longer.

stories.headline: Tan Tock Seng Hospital nearly halves the time to antibiotics for sepsis patients
stories.summary: A nurse-led TTSH initiative called Safe from Sepsis cut the median time to administer antibiotics from 220 minutes to 114 minutes, after training 1,763 nurses to spot patients at risk earlier. Before the programme only 37 per cent of sepsis patients received antibiotics within the 180-minute window that markedly improves survival; the team's target is at least 80 per cent. The hospital plans to extend it to other institutions in the National Healthcare Group cluster.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Tan Tock Seng Hospital)

stories.headline: All residents moved out of two nursing homes months before their licences are revoked
stories.summary: The 25 residents of Windsor Convalescent Home in Pasir Panjang and 78 at LC Nursing Home in Jalan Ulu Siglap were transferred out by Aug 1, well ahead of the Ministry of Health's revocation deadlines of Oct 30 and November respectively, after serious repeated lapses in care and safety. MOH said it oversaw the process with the Agency for Integrated Care and interim operator Vanguard Healthcare. The ministry is separately investigating whether LC Nursing Home's founder failed to disclose prior disciplinary action during licensing.

stories.headline: Singapore and Luxembourg to deepen ties in quantum tech, AI and satellite communications
stories.summary: Hosting Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden at an official lunch, PM Lawrence Wong said the two countries would do more together in 'emerging and critical' areas including quantum computing, artificial intelligence, space and satellite communications. Luxembourg is the largest EU investor in Singapore and Singapore's second-largest investment destination in the bloc. PM Frieden is on a three-day visit from Sept 6, his first as prime minister.

stories.headline: New health guidelines add osteoporosis screening and bring breast cancer scans forward
stories.summary: Updated national screening guidelines recommend osteoporosis screening and move the recommended start of routine mammograms earlier, to age 40. The changes affect what Singaporeans are advised to go for and when.

stories.headline: JTC explores putting light industry and homes in the same building
stories.summary: JTC is working with architects on the idea of stacking industrial space and housing under one roof, testing whether the two uses can share a building in land-scarce Singapore. The work is exploratory rather than a committed project.

stories.headline: Court upholds 11-year jail term for drink driver who severed a pedestrian's body
stories.summary: Appeals by both the defence and the prosecution were dismissed, leaving the original 11-year sentence in place for the driver who struck a 64-year-old retiree crossing Dunearn Road in 2023 at between 111kmh and 122kmh.

stories.headline: Teen sentenced to reformative training for trafficking Kpods and kicking an 84-year-old woman
stories.summary: The teenager was given reformative training for trafficking etomidate-laced vape pods and for kicking an 84-year-old woman. He had also worked as a runner for a money laundering group, withdrawing S$19,000 from six UOB bank accounts.

stories.headline: Prosecution seeks up to 13.5 years' jail and a lifetime driving ban over the fatal Tampines crash
stories.summary: Prosecutors asked for up to 13 years and six months' jail and a lifetime driving ban for the 45-year-old driver in the 2024 Tampines chain collision that killed two people.

stories.headline: Activist Jolovan Wham charged over an assembly at the State Courts and vigils near Changi Prison
stories.summary: Wham was charged with organising a public assembly at the State Courts and attending candlelight vigils near Changi Prison held to mark the executions of three drug traffickers.

stories.headline: Second former EM Services project manager charged over an alleged S$50,000 bribe
stories.summary: A 56-year-old employee of the town council management company is accused of taking a S$50,000 bribe, part of which was allegedly spent on family expenses. He is the second former EM Services project manager to be charged in the case.

stories.headline: Father jailed 14 months for getting his son to understate a luxury watch firm's income
stories.summary: Pang Chuan Wah, 61, was sentenced on Sept 7 for abetting his son to evade tax between 2018 and 2020, causing S$351,787.20 in income tax to be undercharged. In one return he had his son declare sales of S$919,998 when the business had in fact taken S$10.48 million, which would have cost a further S$108,619 in GST. He must pay a penalty of S$1,055,361.60 plus S$371,446.92 to IRAS. His son's case is still before the courts.

stories.headline: Singaporean who ran over a cyclist in Perth pleads guilty to manslaughter
stories.summary: Ng Jing Kai, 29, initially charged with murder, pleaded guilty in August in the Supreme Court of Western Australia to the reduced charge and will be sentenced on Nov 3. Police said he hit the 48-year-old cyclist with a car in the Perth suburb of Carlisle in May 2024 and dragged him, causing fatal injuries; Australian reports said the incident followed an accusation that the cyclist had taken items from the car. Ng has been in custody since his arrest. Manslaughter carries a maximum of life imprisonment.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Western Australia Police Force)

stories.headline: Singaporean arrested in Bangkok is wanted here for drug offences, CNB says
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau said the 41-year-old, arrested on Sept 3 at a Bang Khae condominium, is wanted for investigations into suspected drug offences in Singapore and left the country in September 2023 without returning. Thai police said he was found with crystal methamphetamine, drug paraphernalia and about 200,000 baht (S$7,700) in cash, and that a phone contained evidence of him ordering a poison from the dark web. He has been charged in Thailand with narcotics possession and use and overstaying; investigations into other substances continue.

stories.headline: Man who raped his daughter surrendered after spotting her at a police station
stories.summary: The 51-year-old raped his daughter when she was 15. The court heard he saw her at a police station, went home to change into jeans, and then turned himself in.

stories.headline: Woman accused of taking S$1.7 million from a late businessman says they were lovers
stories.summary: The 39-year-old, accused of embezzling S$1.7 million from a 73-year-old Singaporean businessman who has since died, told the court they had been in a relationship and that the money was a gift.

stories.headline: Briton, 22, given a short detention order for assaulting a private-hire driver who later died
stories.summary: The British man was handed a five-day short detention order and 100 hours of community service for using criminal force on a 66-year-old private-hire driver. The driver has since died.

stories.headline: Woman sues preschool for negligence after her son was pushed off an indoor slide
stories.summary: The boy's parents broke down in court as they watched video of their son clutching his hand and running towards teachers after falling from the indoor slide when another child pushed him. The suit alleges the preschool was negligent.

stories.headline: Luxury goods seized in the S$3 billion money laundering case draw over S$1.3 million in bids
stories.summary: Bidding opened at 10am on Sept 7 on the first two of 15 timed online auctions run by Hotlotz: 338 lots of handbags and accessories, closing Sept 20, and 286 lots of fine jewellery, closing Sept 27. By 5pm the pool of bids exceeded S$1.3 million. A Yayoi Kusama x Louis Vuitton pumpkin bag had drawn 10 bids topping S$18,000, and a 15.02-carat fancy yellow diamond ring stood at S$190,000. Deloitte manages the seized assets, with auctions running to May 2027.

stories.headline: Calvin Cheng joins the debate on Indian nationals and integration
stories.summary: Former Nominated MP Calvin Cheng said in a Sept 6 Facebook post that it is natural for people to stick together, while urging immigrants to assimilate and move out of their comfort zones. He was responding to claims that Indian nationals form exclusive social networks. His post follows racist comments made online about the nine Singaporeans missing in Nepal's floods and about Singapore Airlines' Air India investment - remarks PM Lawrence Wong and SM Lee Hsien Loong urged Singaporeans to reject over the weekend and which SM K. Shanmugam said police would look into.

stories.headline: Singapore celebrity allegedly seen helping run pyramid-scheme meetings in Nanning
stories.summary: Two women who went on organised trips to Nanning in Guangxi told Shin Min Daily News they saw the same male Singapore celebrity at the events, one of them describing him as part of the team welcoming new recruits. MFA said on Sept 4 that 52 Singaporeans had been arrested and detained in Guangxi in a Chinese operation against suspected pyramid-scheme activity. The celebrity has not been named and the accounts have not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Son says his late mother put S$50,000 into an alleged pyramid scheme after a Nanning trip
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man told Shin Min Daily News he is trying to recover S$50,000 his mother invested after a five-day trip to Nanning in 2019, arranged by a man she met at a recreational club who described the city as 'China's Southeast Asia' and covered all costs except airfare. She died in 2023. He described days packed with property visits and 'a constant barrage of information, leaving you no room to think'.

stories.headline: Police turn up at a Yishun getai over a noise complaint, a first in 23 years
stories.summary: Officers arrived at MPC@Khatib about an hour and 20 minutes after the Sept 4 getai began, apparently after a resident complained about the volume. Organising committee chairman Koh Fook Keong told Shin Min Daily News it was the first complaint in the event's 23-year history; the association holds it once a year. Officers spoke to the organisers and the show went on.

stories.headline: Given 30 days to live in 2018, he now runs a Yishun noodle stall with his wife
stories.summary: Chen Yongseng, 48, was diagnosed with late-stage nasopharyngeal carcinoma in 2018 and told he had about 30 days left. He told Shin Min Daily News he went through 37 rounds of chemotherapy and radiotherapy alone, without telling his family, and now runs Xiao Wen Ban Mian at Block 504 Yishun Street 51 with his wife, who married him after the diagnosis.

stories.headline: Woman draws flak over the sleeping space set aside for her helper in a 4-room BTO
stories.summary: A Singaporean woman's post showing the partitioned nook she had set up for her domestic helper in a four-room BTO flat drew criticism online over how small the space was.

stories.headline: Korean chain Seoul Yummy to close its last outlet at Kallang Wave Mall on Oct 22
stories.summary: The chain will shut its final Singapore outlet on Oct 22, ending its run here. It is offering 18 per cent off its signature Korean army stew until then.

stories.headline: Japanese-French patisserie Pantler stays open after a new owner steps in
stories.summary: Pantler will keep trading after a new owner took over, reversing its planned closure.

stories.headline: Blackpink Lisa documentary to screen in Singapore cinemas from Oct 12 to 17
stories.summary: Always Lalisa, a documentary on Blackpink member Lisa, will run in Singapore cinemas for six days from Oct 12.

stories.headline: Mediacorp dating show Wingman premieres on Sept 10
stories.summary: Mediacorp's new dating series Wingman premieres on Sept 10 with a cast that includes actors from around the region.

stories.headline: Amid a 'friendship recession', young Singaporeans are bonding over shared interests
stories.summary: With surveys pointing to fewer close friendships among young adults, some Singaporeans are turning to interest-based groups - run clubs, craft circles, board-game nights - as a route to making friends as adults.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Moscow reopened the door to three-way talks on Monday - Dmitry Peskov said the trilateral format is not ruled out, though it is 'too early' to name a venue - even as BBC Verify found Kyiv logged 76 air raid alerts in a single week, more than at any point since the invasion began. That gap between the negotiating track and the air war runs through every theatre. In the Gulf the shift was less military than political: the UAE and Qatar answered Iran's threats against American energy assets not by picking a side but by saying out loud that Washington's protection is no longer enough - the development most likely to outlast any ceasefire. Lebanon stayed the deadliest front, and Israel widened its threats to the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank. Nothing is moving towards a settlement; the fronts are being reinforced while negotiators talk.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Talks are edging back towards a format while the air war gets worse. The Kremlin said on 7 September it does not rule out resuming trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington after the Witkoff-Kushner shuttle, though Dmitry Peskov called it too early to name a venue or dates and Volodymyr Zelensky has said he expects fighting into the winter. Against that, BBC Verify's analysis of Ukrainian government data found Kyiv logged 76 air raid alerts in the seven days from 27 August - more than at any point since 2022 - as Russia shifts to round-the-clock daytime attacks with faster jet-powered drones. The sabotage campaign against European infrastructure continues, with 21 explosive devices now recovered near power lines in Saxony, and Moscow has hardened its language over the US missile deployment in Norway. All strike, casualty and attribution claims here are those of parties to the war or their governments.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia kill at least 10 people according to Russian regional officials and halt work at a warehouse of the online retailer Ozon in the Samara region. Russia's figures are not independently verified.

The death toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih rises to 16, with 130 injured and four people still missing, says Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue work may run for two more days.
President Vladimir Putin says Ukraine has opened a 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia will hit back at Ukraine's 'most sensitive economic sectors'.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, visiting Ukraine, condemns what he calls Russia's escalating attacks on civilian areas.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to accelerate deliveries of French air-defence equipment, after Kyiv said a shortage of interceptors was costing lives. Paris has not published a delivery schedule.

Norway's government says it will give Ukraine another 85 billion Norwegian crowns (about US$9.2 billion) in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year, matching its 2026 contribution and split between military and humanitarian spending. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere announced it while visiting Kyiv with Nordic and Baltic leaders.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine believes Russia plans to draft an additional 300,000 troops after Russian parliamentary elections in mid-September, working towards 500,000 overall by 2027, and that Moscow is raising missile production to about 1,300 a year. These are Ukrainian assessments and have not been independently verified; the Kremlin has not confirmed them.

Zelensky rejects holding a wartime election, saying a vote during this kind of war would 'destroy' the country by splitting Ukrainians. It is his first response to ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a poll. Elections in war are prohibited by Ukrainian law and the country has been under martial law since 2022.

Sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov tells the BBC that Zelensky should be asked what he knew about corruption in his government, following a money-laundering investigation announced last week, while saying he never saw the president act corruptly and never received an improper instruction from him. He repeats his call for a wartime vote.

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store says Norway will give Ukraine US$9 billion (about S$11.4 billion) in 2027, matching this year's record level, with most of it going to the military. Baltic and Nordic leaders gather in Kyiv for a summit with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky says Ukraine's army faces a US$27 billion deficit and urges the European Union to advance payments on part of a 90 billion euro loan, warning that without about US$10 billion by the end of the year his soldiers will not have enough weapons. He did not give a detailed breakdown.

Ozon reports a fire at its logistics hub in Russia's central Orenburg region after a drone attack and suspends warehouse operations, a day after an Ozon centre in the neighbouring Samara region was hit and an unspecified number of workers wounded.
A Russian attack on the outskirts of the north-eastern city of Kharkiv kills three people, the regional governor says on Telegram.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev says drone debris hit a private childcare centre overnight, killing two children and injuring nine people including seven children, and that debris fell on apartment buildings. The Russian account is not independently verified.

Ozon says a 'major fire' is burning at one of its logistics centres in the Krasnodar region after a drone attack, the second consecutive day one of its hubs has been hit. The company says staff were evacuated and there are preliminarily no casualties. Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 Aug it was extending to Ozon a campaign that has already struck the 15 largest Wildberries logistics hubs.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ozon, Ukrainian defence ministry)

timeline.event: A drone attack on an industrial area in Nevinnomysk, a chemical production centre in the Stavropol region, is repelled, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov says on Telegram.
Zelensky says Ukraine was not behind the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts and that Kyiv is cooperating with the German-led investigation, after two arrests in the case.

Kyiv hosts a meeting of the French- and British-led Coalition of the Willing to discuss stepping up support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia ahead of winter, as Ukraine marks 35 years of independence.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is due to urge US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to take a more active role on Ukraine, The Straits Times reports.
President Volodymyr Zelensky marks 35 years of Ukrainian independence, saying Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russian terms.
BBC reports that President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday Ukraine had opened 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's most sensitive economic sectors.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says measures are being taken to minimise the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia's grain exports, telling reporters that 'all grain intended for export' will be shipped on time and in full. Tit-for-tat attacks on ports and vessels have shuttered grain terminals and forced dozens of cargoes to be delayed or cancelled in peak export season.

Zelensky says Russia is 'not ready' for a ceasefire limited to attacks on Black Sea ships carrying agricultural produce, because Moscow wants any deal extended to cover strikes on Russian refineries and pipelines.

Ukrainian drone strikes set fire to logistics centres belonging to Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, in Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea. The BBC verified video of the attacks. Ozon said several people were injured; Russia's defence ministry said three children aged 13, 15 and 16 were killed in Krasnodar. Neither account has been independently verified. Ozon shares fell as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange and those of its main shareholder AFK Sistema by almost 13%.

Andy Burnham, on his first overseas trip as UK prime minister, met Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the British- and French-led coalition of the willing. Britain agreed to hand over blueprints for UK-made components of the Scalp missile, the French version of the Storm Shadow cruise missile, so Ukraine can build the weapon domestically. Burnham urged the US Congress to 'ratchet up' economic pressure on Russia.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the British missile transfer prevented 'even the slightest progress' towards peace and that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate and destroy any Ukrainian missile production sites. Asked about the charge that Britain was adding fuel to the fire, Burnham replied: 'Who started the fire?'
Ukrainian strikes hit Russia's second-biggest online retailer, extending Kyiv's campaign against Russian commercial and logistics infrastructure.
Britain and Ukraine signed an artificial-intelligence defence partnership covering battlefield technology, extending the industrial cooperation announced during Burnham's visit.

President Vladimir Putin granted the Russian state the right to take control of infrastructure it judges inadequately protected against drone attacks, a response to Ukraine's deepening campaign against Russian economic targets.
Britain and France pledged stronger support as Ukraine marked 35 years of independence, with Burnham saying allies were digging into their own stocks of air defences to help protect Ukrainian skies.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev said the Afipsky oil refinery was on fire after a drone attack, and that two people were killed and two injured by falling drone debris at the Afipsky railway station. The account is from Russian regional officials and is not independently verified. The export-focused plant processed about 144,000 barrels a day in 2024, and follows the halt of the Perm refinery after a Ukrainian drone strike on 21 August.

Andrei Fedorov, an adviser to the Kremlin, told BBC Newsnight there might be a 'semi-military' response against UK drone factories by 'unknown sources' over Britain sharing blueprints for Scalp/Storm Shadow missile components. The remark is one adviser's and not a stated Russian government position.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, returning from Kyiv, said he will 'likely' travel to the United States next month with European leaders to lobby President Trump on Ukraine's defence needs, though he said the details were not fully confirmed. It would be his first US trip since taking office in July.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican's foreign minister, met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow — the first in-person Vatican-Russia talks in five years. Gallagher said it was 'urgent and necessary' to end the war, and the two agreed to cooperate on humanitarian matters including children affected by the fighting.

A US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster, tail number 07-7181, flew direct from Riga and landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at about 0700 GMT, per Flightradar24 data. It is the first direct flight of a US-registered jet to Russia from Europe since January. The Kremlin said it had no information on the plane; its cargo and passengers could not be verified.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine sees a window for US-led mediation until the end of next summer, and that a one-page set of ideas drafted with US and European officials — a ceasefire as the main point, plus a US-proposed free economic zone in Donbas administered by a third party — will be put to Moscow.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Finnish President Alexander Stubb's approval of Ukrainian long-range strikes inside Russia showed he belonged, alongside Britain's Andy Burnham, to the 'party of war', and accused Western leaders of misleading voters about Russia being strategically defeated.

German investigators found a third drone west of Leipzig/Halle Airport on 14 August, 10 days after the attempted attack, along with about 50g of a substance suspected to be the military explosive hexogen, according to NDR, WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung. Security sources cited in the reports suspect Russian intelligence involvement; Moscow denies it. The prosecutor-general's office did not comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (NDR, WDR, Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

timeline.event: Sweden's military said it was seeking to take over a Russian-owned estate close to a Swedish naval base, citing security concerns.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that whoever was behind a drone incident over Germany would 'pay a price'. No party has been formally identified.
Slovak police said they had thwarted a planned arson attack on a drone factory.

German magazine Der Spiegel reported that a man detained over a Berlin gun stash is suspected of being part of a Russian network. The claim comes from the magazine's reporting and has not been confirmed by prosecutors.
Mykhailo Fedorov, recently ousted as defence minister, said Ukraine needs to change how it is fighting to avoid losing the war.

The United States asked Ukraine not to launch air strikes around Moscow, St Petersburg and some northern Russian territories on 24, 25 and 26 August, because a plane carrying a senior US official would be in the area.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow for meetings with Russian officials, CBS News and Axios reported citing unnamed sources — the first known Moscow visit by a US intelligence chief since William Burns met Vladimir Putin in November 2021. The CIA declined to comment; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov neither confirmed nor denied the visit and said Putin had no plans to meet Ratcliffe.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, CNA (CBS News, Axios)

timeline.event: Switzerland will hold a referendum next month on adopting a more restrictive form of neutrality that would bar it from imposing economic sanctions or cooperating with NATO in peacetime.

The BBC reports the CIA director's Moscow trip would be the first known visit by a US spy chief since 2021. The CIA declined to comment and the Kremlin said President Vladimir Putin had no plans to meet him.

The Kremlin said CIA director John Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence counterparts during his Moscow visit, while stating that President Vladimir Putin did not meet him. Neither side described what was discussed.
A Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region was destroyed by fire after being hit by a drone, the regional governor said. Ukraine did not claim the strike.
The BBC reported that as Ukraine keeps striking Russian oil refineries, Russia has shifted to targeting Ukraine's fuel distribution network, including petrol stations.
Ukraine awarded Elon Musk a high state honour as Kyiv seeks to expand its use of Starlink.
The Kremlin said remarks by ousted Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov showed Kyiv was consumed by infighting. The characterisation is Moscow's; Kyiv has not responded.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that those behind a drone incident over German territory would 'pay a price'. Berlin has not publicly attributed the incident.

Ukraine's military named prominent commanders to lead the defence of the eastern region that Russia is demanding be ceded in any settlement, signalling it intends to hold the ground rather than trade it.

President Donald Trump described CIA director John Ratcliffe's unannounced Moscow trip as a 'semi-routine' mission and said 'something may come out of' it. Neither Washington nor Moscow has said what was discussed.
A US senator said he hoped a 'sledgehammer' package of Russian sanctions would pass Congress next month. The bill has not been scheduled for a vote.
A Pentagon official is to brief NATO allies as a US force-posture review raises questions among European members about the scale of the American commitment to the continent.
France's security chief said he sees new threats following the drone attack at Leipzig. No attribution for that incident has been made public by German or French authorities.

The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported that CIA director John Ratcliffe used his Moscow visit to warn Russia against attacking NATO members, following US intelligence assessments that Moscow could seek to test the alliance. Neither the White House nor the Kremlin has confirmed the content of the talks.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (WSJ, CBS News)

timeline.event: US officials said the Pentagon's global posture review is preparing options on American troop levels in Europe for Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth by 6 November. No decision has been announced.

Russia launched a large overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. Ukraine's air force said the barrage included two Oniks anti-ship cruise missiles, 258 drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, and that nearly 90 per cent of the drones were downed along with one Oniks and seven ballistic missiles. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said ports, grain storage, energy and industrial infrastructure were targeted.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrainian Air Force, Ukrainian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky said European allies had made 'important decisions' this week to strengthen Ukrainian air defence and that Ukraine had recently received a small batch of Patriot interceptors, renewing his call for further packages. Kyiv has been short of the US-made interceptors capable of downing ballistic missiles.
Russia said it could strike British military targets in response to Ukraine's use of British-supplied missiles against Russian territory.
A senior aide to President Volodymyr Zelensky said talks between Ukraine and Russia may be possible in September.
Russia's foreign intelligence chief confirmed that he held talks with CIA director John Ratcliffe during the American's unannounced visit to Moscow. Neither government has said what was discussed.

US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby, visiting NATO headquarters in Brussels, pressed European allies to set out how they are taking primary responsibility for the continent's conventional defence, as Washington's six-month review of its force posture in Europe continues.
Slovak prosecutors said suspects had planned an arson attack on Skyeton, a Ukrainian drone manufacturer.
Bulgaria will receive seven minehunter ships from Belgium and the Netherlands to help protect the Black Sea.
An EU official said there were no signs Russia is preparing a military attack on NATO countries, pushing back on warnings circulating in allied capitals.

The Netherlands, Poland, Spain and Sweden called for the European Union to reopen discussion next week on using Russia's frozen assets for Ukraine, arguing Moscow shows no sign of wanting to end the war. Belgium, which holds most of the assets, has previously blocked the idea.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Dutch, Polish, Spanish and Swedish governments)

timeline.event: Poland's deputy defence minister said Poland does not want nuclear warheads stationed on its territory.
A car bomb killed a Russian army officer outside Saint Petersburg, Russian media reported. No one has claimed responsibility and investigators have not publicly attributed the attack.

President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin will not attack NATO territory and played down reports that CIA director John Ratcliffe had warned Russian officials against doing so during his unannounced Moscow visit.
Authorities in Ukraine's Kherson told residents to leave the city, the strongest evacuation message from the regional administration in recent weeks.

Ukrainian courier company Nova Poshta said Russian attacks destroyed its sorting centres near Kyiv and in the northern city of Sumy. It said four guided aerial bombs hit the Sumy terminal and damaged three trucks, that all employees were unharmed, and that it continued to operate.
Sweden's military will help survey and protect Finnish territory with Gripen fighter jets and a corvette, at least until the end of 2026, Finland's defence forces said.
Countries bordering the Baltic Sea plan a joint task force for drone defence so they can react quickly to hybrid attacks, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said in Flensburg.

The Straits Times reported, citing officials, that CIA director John Ratcliffe's 25 August trip to Moscow was an attempt to persuade the Russian leadership against fresh provocations in Europe. The account is single-sourced reporting and has not been confirmed by either government.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States had passed Kyiv information about a number of meetings held in Moscow over the previous few days, following CIA director John Ratcliffe's trip to the Russian capital on 25 August.
Ukraine's top presidential adviser said technical talks on the war would likely take place in the near future, while cautioning that he did not expect a swift agreement.
Mykhailo Fedorov, dismissed as Ukraine's defence chief six weeks earlier, agreed to become adviser on defence innovation to Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto.

Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks across the country killed 16 people and injured 50 over the previous day, with strikes reported on a gas station in Kharkiv, a supermarket in Pavlohrad and warehouses in the Kyiv region. The tallies come from Ukrainian regional authorities and have not been independently verified; Russia's defence ministry says it targets military and military-linked infrastructure.

Zelensky said Ukraine's security service struck a Tu-95MS missile carrier at Engels airbase and that Ukrainian forces hit an oil refinery in Russia's Yaroslavl region. Both are Ukrainian claims; Moscow has not confirmed the damage.
Ukraine's military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov said Ukraine needs to mobilise at least 30,000 people a month, and separately that ending the war now is unrealistic.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says the United States passed Kyiv information about a number of meetings held in Moscow over recent days, thanking Washington for the information and for "the necessary tone of the conversation with Russia", without saying who took part.

Western officials told the BBC that Russia is sharpening its rhetoric towards NATO but wants to avoid a direct war with the alliance, while remaining likely to continue hybrid activity against member states short of open military action.

Ukraine's Air Force said air defences neutralised 233 of 267 attack drones launched from the evening of 28 August, in a barrage that also included an Oniks anti-ship missile and an Iskander-M ballistic missile fired from occupied Crimea. The figures are Ukrainian military claims and have not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said after a Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters meeting that Ukraine's goal is 1,000 long-range strike drones a day against Russia, against an average of 300 or more now.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service said a Russian strike in the Odesa region killed one person and injured three, setting eight lorries carrying food on fire; an overnight attack on the Izmail district damaged transport infrastructure. Both accounts come from Ukrainian authorities.

Ukraine's General Staff reported 242 combat clashes along the front over the previous day, the largest number of them on the Pokrovsk axis. Russia's defence ministry gives its own, differing accounts of front-line activity.
The leaders of Russia, China and Iran are due to attend a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, a bloc that presents itself as a counterweight to Western influence.

A Russian drone struck an enterprise in the town of Myla, in Kyiv region's Bucha district, at about 8.10pm on 28 August, causing a large fire and sustained detonations. Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko reported 27 dead and more than 40 wounded during the afternoon; Ukrinform reported the toll had risen to 37 by evening and the BBC reported hundreds of residents evacuated. Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, was among the dead. All figures are Ukrainian officials' and are not independently verified.

Ukraine's prosecutor general opened a criminal negligence investigation into the Myla site, saying it would examine the legality of storing explosive objects and materials on the enterprise's grounds and whether the company held the necessary permits. Officials did not describe the nature of the facility.
A mass drone attack caused a local blackout in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, leaving about 300,000 customers without power, Ukrinform reported citing Ukrainian authorities.

Ukraine's Defence Forces said they struck launch sites used for Russian attack drones in Donetsk region and occupied Crimea, and separately that drones hit an Ozon logistics centre in Russia's Rostov region. Both are Ukrainian claims; Moscow has not confirmed the damage.
Estonia's foreign minister called for increased pressure on Russia following the overnight attack on Ukraine.

The death toll from the Russian drone strike on a weapons store at Myla, in Kyiv region's Bucha district, reaches 37 with 42 injured, four of them children. Regional head Tymur Tkachenko says around 80 sites were damaged and about 130 homes hit; police say four people are still missing. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted an ammunition depot holding components for long-range drones.

Zelensky says the store "definitely shouldn't have been there" and orders an investigation into "terrible negligence" by whoever kept explosives beside houses; Ukraine's defence ministry separately calls on defence-industry leaders to audit how they store weapons and ammunition.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 224 attack drones between 6.30am and 6pm, most of them jet-powered and the majority aimed at Kyiv, and that 199 were shot down or jammed. The figures are Ukrainian and not independently verified.

A two-year-old girl dies in hospital of shrapnel wounds after drone debris falls in a park in Kyiv's Obolon district, and eight people are injured in the capital during the day, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says. A second strike hits a non-residential building in the Podil district.

The IAEA says the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has been without off-site power for more than a week and is running its cooling on emergency diesel generators with only a 10-day fuel supply, after military activity on the northern side of the Dnipro. Director General Rafael Grossi calls reliable external power "indispensable"; the agency is seeking a local ceasefire to repair the lines and reports three drone incidents at the site this week that injured two employees.

Finland's President Alexander Stubb tells Germany's Bild he sees "neither evidence nor facts" behind assessments that Russia could attack a NATO country by 2029, saying it would "make no sense" for Moscow to test the alliance. German officials have made that 2029 assessment.
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk says after talks with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that Ukraine needs greater air support amid Russian escalation.
Kyiv region declares 30 August a day of mourning for the victims of the Myla blast, with flags at half-mast and entertainment venues restricted, regional administration head Tymur Tkachenko says.
Putin and Xi Jinping are due in Bishkek on 31 August for a two-day Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit marking the bloc's 25 years, also attended by the leaders of Iran and India.

Ukraine's General Staff says 221 combat engagements were recorded along the front in the previous 24 hours, with the heaviest fighting in the Kostiantynivka sector (31 Russian attacks) and the Pokrovsk sector (30). Russian figures are not available and the tallies are not independently verified.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least three people were injured in a drone attack on Kyiv, with a fire running from the second to the fifth floor of a 12-storey residential block in Obolonskyi district and damage in three other districts. The service says eight people were injured in the capital across the wider attack, three of them hospitalised. Not independently verified.

The head of the Kherson regional military administration, Oleksandr Prokudin, says Russian attacks killed three people and wounded 17 across the region in 24 hours, damaging six high-rise buildings and 14 private homes. Not independently verified.
Russian forces struck warehouses in the city of Zaporizhzhia in a morning attack, starting a fire, regional officials say.

Ukraine's General Staff issues a public warning against siting ammunition depots near civilian areas, a day after the Myla blast, and the defence ministry asks defence-industry leaders to audit how they store weapons and ammunition.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian General Staff, Ukraine's defence ministry)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky says the death toll from the 28 August strike on the ammunition depot at Myla in Kyiv region has risen to 38, with four people still missing; Ukrinform reports 20 injured. Zelensky says most fires have been put out but contamination of the site is significant. It is the deadliest Russian strike in the Kyiv area this year.

Zelensky says Russia launched nearly 2,000 strike drones, more than 1,600 aerial bombs and 31 missiles at Ukraine over the past week, including North Korean ballistic missiles. The figures are Ukrainian and are not independently verified.
Ukraine's air defence forces say they shot down 125 Russian drones overnight. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's Defence Forces say they struck the Kirishi oil refinery and the Yeysk airfield inside Russia, and separately claim the destruction of five Russian air defence assets at the Yeysk and Millerovo airfields. Ukrainian claims; Russia has not confirmed them.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Defence Forces, Unmanned Systems Forces)

timeline.event: Ukrainian forces deny Russian claims to have captured Velykyi Prykil and Sadky in the Sumy region. Both sides' battlefield claims remain unverified.

A Russian attack on the Odesa region injures at least three people overnight, and drones and 'Banderole' missiles strike port infrastructure in the Mykolaiv region, Ukrainian regional authorities say.
Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces say they destroyed five Russian air-defence assets at the Yeysk and Millerovo airfields inside Russia. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.
Two people, including a minor, are killed in a Russian guided-bomb strike on the Donetsk region, regional authorities say.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says Berlin is finalising a response, coordinated with European and NATO partners, to the suspected drone attack on a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport on 4 August. Germany has not officially attributed the incident.
A NATO official says the alliance sees no imminent threat of an attack, The Straits Times reports.
Ukraine's defence chief pledges to set out a clear war plan as Kyiv seeks the early release of loan funding, The Straits Times reports.

Kyiv regional authorities raise the number of casualties from the 28 August strike on the ammunition depot at Myla to 52, including five children; 38 of them have died. Ukrainian figures, not independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia launched nearly 1,500 drones of all types at Ukraine over four days, about 800 of them jet-powered. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 186 combat clashes along the front over the past day, with more than 40 Russian attacks repelled in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors combined - down from 221 clashes the day before. Ukrainian claim.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says a trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin would be possible "only to formalize agreements".
Russian attacks injure four people in the Dnipropetrovsk region over the course of a day, with the region struck nearly 50 times, regional authorities say.

Russia attacked overnight with one Kh-59 guided missile and 121 Shahed-type attack, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, the Ukrainian Air Force Command says; air defences shot down or suppressed 96 drones and the missile did not reach its target, with hits recorded at 11 locations. Ukrainian military claim.
Ukraine's General Staff reports 225 combat clashes over the past 24 hours, the most in the Pokrovsk sector, alongside 91 Russian airstrikes dropping 288 guided bombs. Ukrainian military claim.
Two people were killed and three injured as Russian forces carried out 923 strikes on the Zaporizhzhia region over the past day, regional authorities say. Ukrainian regional claim.

A missile attack on the Russian city of Belgorod killed two people and injured 16, acting governor Alexander Shuvayev says, after a Ukrainian strike on a commercial facility set seven warehouses ablaze; Russian retailer Ozon says a logistics hub and a sorting facility were hit. Russian official claim.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Belgorod acting governor, Ozon)

timeline.event: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says NATO's moves in the Arctic pose a "direct threat" to Russia; NATO said separately it sees no imminent threat of attack.

Russian drone attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region stretch into a fifth day, with near round-the-clock air raid sirens disrupting daily life; attacks early on Monday injure four people and damage warehouses, an apartment block and a retail outlet, regional governor Tymur Tkachenko says. Ukrainian official account.

Six people are injured in drone attacks on Kyiv and the village of Pohreby, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says; three are hospitalised in serious condition and warehouse facilities in Pohreby catch fire. Ukrainian official claim.

Energy company DTEK says Russian forces have attacked its Dnipropetrovsk region facilities three times in recent days; power was restored to 40,000 customers over two days but another 30,000 remain without electricity. Company statement.
Ukraine's Defence Forces say they struck a Russian radar, an S-400 command-and-staff vehicle and supply depots. Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the oil tanker MV Sun, suspected of sailing under a false flag, was boarded on 30 August in the Mediterranean by EUNAVFOR MED IRINI forces for flag verification — the sixth suspected Russian shadow-fleet vessel boarded by EU operations in recent months. Shadow-fleet action is on the agenda when EU defence ministers meet in Ireland on Tuesday.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pledges a "swift response" to Russian hybrid attacks; separately, Polish authorities are investigating possible sabotage after a fire at a Polish drone manufacturer.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 173 combat clashes along the front on 31 August, with 66 Russian airstrikes dropping 218 guided glide bombs, 6,542 kamikaze drones deployed and 2,049 attacks on settlements and positions. The heaviest fighting was again in the Pokrovsk sector, where 32 assaults were repelled and, by preliminary Ukrainian estimates, 53 Russian troops were killed and 18 wounded. Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

The Kherson Regional Prosecutor's Office says three civilians were killed and seven injured, including an 11-year-old boy, in Russian artillery and drone attacks across the region during the day. A 65-year-old woman in Kostyrka was killed by a drone strike; a Russian drone also hit a supermarket roof in Kherson, injuring a child. War-crimes investigations have been opened. Ukrainian official account.

The Kyiv Regional Military Administration says nine people were injured in Russian air attacks in the Kyiv region during the day, eight of them in the village of Pohreby, with warehouses damaged in three districts and two houses damaged in Bucha district. Ukrainian official account.

Polish prosecutors open a terrorism investigation into a fire at the WB Electronics drone factory in Skarzysko-Kamienna, saying it was started deliberately with a device containing flammable materials, and also investigating “participation in the activities of a foreign intelligence service directed against the Republic of Poland”. No suspect has been named; Poland has repeatedly accused Russia of sabotage since 2022 and Moscow has denied it.

Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attends a G20 finance ministers' meeting in Asheville, North Carolina in person — his first since the 2022 invasion — after a US invitation, and holds a bilateral meeting with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that a US official says focused on President Trump's Ukraine peace plan.
